sc: Child from Kordofan, jaundice since 7 months, painful swollen hands and feet → HbSS: Hb electrophoresis
2-year-old with HbSS, sudden pallor, fast pulse, spleen suddenly large → Splenic sequestration: urgent transfusion
HbSS with fever, chest pain, new infiltrate → Acute chest syndrome
f: Dactylitis (first sign, 6 months–2 yr) · painful crises · anaemia, jaundice · infections (hyposplenism) · stroke
Hb electrophoresis (HPLC) · sickling test (screen only) · film: sickle cells, Howell–Jolly bodies (autosplenectomy by 5–6 yr)
Painful crisis · acute chest syndrome · stroke · splenic sequestration · aplastic crisis (parvovirus, low retics) · sepsis · priapism
Pain: fluids, analgesia, morphine 0.1 mg/kg · fever ≥ 38.5 °C: IV ceftriaxone · sequestration: transfuse 5–10 ml/kg · stroke: exchange transfusion (HbS < 30%)
Penicillin to 5 years, vaccines (pneumococcal), folic acid · hydroxyurea from 9 months (20 mg/kg/day) · yearly TCD 2–16 yr
Avascular necrosis of the hip · nephropathy (enuresis) · gallstones · leg ulcers · osteomyelitis (Salmonella)
trap: An uncomplicated painful crisis is not an indication for transfusion · aplastic crisis: pallor without more jaundice, low retics · sickle cell trait is symptom-free and protects against malaria
